facts: Start with a base arm, then place the protractor centre on its endpoint with $0^{\circ}$ along the arm.
Mark a dot at the required degree, then rule the second arm through it.
For reflex angles (greater than $180^{\circ}$ and less than $360^{\circ}$), draw the inner angle $360^{\circ} -$ (reflex) and mark the outside.
steps: Draw a base arm and place the protractor centre on its end.
Find the required degree and mark a point.
Join the vertex to the point with a ruler.

workedExamples.question_text: You are constructing a $135^{\circ}$ angle from a base arm pointing right. One protractor mark has paired readings $45$ and $135$. Explain which scale to use and how to finish the construction.
Use a semicircular protractor to construct a reflex angle of $250^{\circ}$. State the smaller angle you construct first.
Describe how to begin constructing a $100^{\circ}$ angle with a protractor. Give the three essential alignment and drawing checks.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Draw a base arm and mark its endpoint as the vertex. Place the protractor centre on the vertex, with its zero line along the base arm. Follow the scale starting at that zero and mark $100^{\circ}$. Rule the second arm through the mark.

Check that the protractor centre is on the vertex, zero is aligned with the base arm, and the second arm starts at the same vertex and passes through the degree mark.

foundation.question_text:
Using a protractor, construct a $30^{\circ}$ angle from the base arm.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]\coordinate(V)at(0,0);\coordinate(A)at(4,0);\draw(V)--(A);\fill(V)circle(1.5pt)node[below]{$V$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
foundation.solution_text:
Centre the protractor at $V$, mark $30^{\circ}$ from the base arm, then rule the second arm through the mark.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]\usetikzlibrary{angles,quotes}\coordinate(V)at(0,0);\coordinate(A)at(4,0);\coordinate(B)at(30:4);\draw(A)--(V)--(B);\pic[draw,"$30^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.8cm,angle eccentricity=2]{angle=A--V--B};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

foundation.question_text:
Using a protractor, construct a $55^{\circ}$ angle from the base arm.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]\coordinate(V)at(0,0);\draw(V)--(4,0);\fill(V)circle(1.5pt)node[below]{$V$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
foundation.solution_text:
Align $0^{\circ}$ with the base arm, mark $55^{\circ}$, then draw the second arm from $V$ through the mark.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]\usetikzlibrary{angles,quotes}\coordinate(V)at(0,0);\coordinate(A)at(4,0);\coordinate(B)at(55:4);\draw(A)--(V)--(B);\pic[draw,"$55^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.8cm,angle eccentricity=2]{angle=A--V--B};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

foundation.question_text:
Using a protractor, construct a $90^{\circ}$ angle from the base arm.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]\coordinate(V)at(0,0);\draw(V)--(4,0);\fill(V)circle(1.5pt)node[below]{$V$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
foundation.solution_text:
Mark $90^{\circ}$ and rule the second arm through the mark.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]\usetikzlibrary{calc}\coordinate(V)at(0,0);\coordinate(A)at(4,0);\coordinate(B)at(0,4);\draw(A)--(V)--(B);\coordinate(a)at($(V)!0.4cm!(A)$);\coordinate(b)at($(V)!0.4cm!(B)$);\draw(a)--($(a)+(b)-(V)$)--(b);\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

foundation.question_text:
Using a protractor, construct a $110^{\circ}$ angle from the base arm.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]\coordinate(V)at(0,0);\draw(V)--(4,0);\fill(V)circle(1.5pt)node[below]{$V$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
foundation.solution_text:
Use the scale starting at $0^{\circ}$ on the base arm, mark $110^{\circ}$, and draw through it.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]\usetikzlibrary{angles,quotes}\coordinate(V)at(0,0);\coordinate(A)at(4,0);\coordinate(B)at(110:4);\draw(A)--(V)--(B);\pic[draw,"$110^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.8cm,angle eccentricity=2]{angle=A--V--B};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

foundation.question_text:
Using a protractor, construct a $145^{\circ}$ angle from the base arm.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]\coordinate(V)at(0,0);\draw(V)--(4,0);\fill(V)circle(1.5pt)node[below]{$V$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
foundation.solution_text:
Mark $145^{\circ}$ on the scale beginning at the base arm's zero, then rule the second arm.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]\usetikzlibrary{angles,quotes}\coordinate(V)at(0,0);\coordinate(A)at(4,0);\coordinate(B)at(145:4);\draw(A)--(V)--(B);\pic[draw,"$145^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.8cm,angle eccentricity=2]{angle=A--V--B};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

foundation.question_text:
Using a protractor, construct a straight angle from the base arm.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]\coordinate(V)at(0,0);\draw(V)--(4,0);\fill(V)circle(1.5pt)node[below]{$V$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
foundation.solution_text:
Place the second arm directly opposite the base arm.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]\coordinate(V)at(0,0);\draw(-4,0)--(V)--(4,0);\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
The completed angle is $180^{\circ}$.

development.question_text:
Construct a $70^{\circ}$ angle clockwise below the base arm.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]\coordinate(V)at(0,0);\draw(V)--(4,0);\fill(V)circle(1.5pt)node[above]{$V$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
development.solution_text: Use the scale increasing clockwise from the base arm, mark $70^{\circ}$ below it, and join the mark to $V$.

development.question_text:
The base arm is tilted.
Construct a $65^{\circ}$ angle anticlockwise from it.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]\coordinate(V)at(0,0);\draw(V)--(20:4);\fill(V)circle(1.5pt)node[below]{$V$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
development.solution_text: Align the protractor zero line with the tilted arm, mark $65^{\circ}$ anticlockwise, then draw the second arm.

development.question_text:
Construct a reflex angle of $220^{\circ}$.
What smaller angle should you construct first?
development.solution_text:
$360^{\circ}-220^{\circ}$
$=140^{\circ}$
Construct $140^{\circ}$, then mark the outside reflex angle as $220^{\circ}$.

development.question_text:
Construct a reflex angle of $310^{\circ}$.
What smaller angle should you construct first?
development.solution_text:
$360^{\circ}-310^{\circ}$
$=50^{\circ}$
Construct $50^{\circ}$, then identify the outside turn as $310^{\circ}$.

development.question_text:
A target angle is $125^{\circ}$.
The protractor mark shows paired readings $55$ and $125$.
Which reading should be followed?
development.solution_text: Use the reading on the scale that starts at $0^{\circ}$ on the base arm. For the obtuse target, use $125^{\circ}$.

development.question_text:
A learner marks the correct degree but draws the second arm from a point beside the vertex.
Identify the construction error.
development.solution_text: The second arm must begin at the vertex and pass through the degree mark. Starting beside the vertex means the two arms do not share the required vertex.

mastery.question_text: Describe how to construct a $275^{\circ}$ reflex angle with a semicircular protractor.
mastery.solution_text:
$360^{\circ}-275^{\circ}$
$=85^{\circ}$
Construct the $85^{\circ}$ inner angle, then mark the outside angle as $275^{\circ}$.

mastery.question_text:
A $130^{\circ}$ construction is accidentally drawn using the paired $50^{\circ}$ reading.
Explain the error and correction.
mastery.solution_text: The wrong protractor scale was used. Keep the base arm at the scale's $0^{\circ}$ and use the $130^{\circ}$ mark.

mastery.question_text: List the three essential alignment and drawing checks for a protractor construction.
mastery.solution_text: Centre on the vertex; zero line along the base arm; second arm ruled from the vertex through the degree mark.
